questions.text:
Let A and B be two nxn matrices over real numbers. Let rank(M) and det(M) denote the rank and determinant of a matrix M, respectively. Consider the following statements.

I. rank(AB)=rank (A)rank (B)
II. det(AB)=det(A)det(B)
III. rank(A+B) [latex]\leq[/latex] rank (A) + rank (B)
IV. det(A+B) [latex]\leq[/latex] det(A) + det(B)

Which of the above statements are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Use A = B = I (n = 2):
- I: rank(AB) = 2 but rank(A)rank(B) = 4 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: det(AB) = det(A)det(B) is always true [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- III: rank is subadditive: [latex]rank(A+B)\le rank(A)+rank(B)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- IV: det(2I) = 4 [latex]\gt[/latex] det(I) + det(I) = 2 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: II and III only

questions.text:
Consider the functions

I. [latex]e^{-x}[/latex]
II. [latex]x^2-\sin x[/latex]
III. [latex]\sqrt{x^3+1}[/latex]

Which of the above functions is/are increasing everywhere in [0,1] ?
questions.solution:
Check the derivative on [0, 1]:
- I: [latex](e^{-x})'=-e^{-x} \lt 0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decreasing.
- II: [latex]2x-\cos x[/latex] is [latex]-1[/latex] at x = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decreasing near 0.
- III: [latex]\frac{3x^2}{2\sqrt{x^3+1}}\ge0[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] increasing on the whole interval.

Answer: III only

questions.text:
Consider the following matrix:
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 4 & 8\\ 1& 3 & 9 &27 \\ 1 & 4 & 16 &64 \\ 1 & 5 & 25 &125 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
The absolute value of the product of Eigenvalues of R is _________ .
questions.solution:
Product of eigenvalues = determinant. The matrix is a Vandermonde matrix with values 2, 3, 4, 5:
[latex]\det=\prod_{i \lt j}(x_j-x_i)=(3-2)(4-2)(5-2)(4-3)(5-3)(5-4)=1\cdot2\cdot3\cdot1\cdot2\cdot1=12[/latex]

Answer: 12
